input:
General solution of the differential equation cos x(1 + cos y)dx - sin y(1 + sin x)dy = 0 is

Options:
A. (1 + cos x)(1 + sin y) = c
B. 1 + sin x + cos y = c
C. (1 + sin x)(1 + cos y) = c
D. 1 + sin x · cos y = c

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Find the general solution of the given separable differential equation by separating variables and integrating both sides.

given_information.equation: cos x(1 + cos y)dx - sin y(1 + sin x)dy = 0

phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Rearrange to separate x and y: cos x/(1+sin x) dx = sin y/(1+cos y) dy. Each side can be integrated directly since numerator is derivative of denominator (up to sign).

key_concepts: Integration of f'(x)/f(x) form: ∫f'/f dx = log|f| + c
Logarithm laws for combining log terms

key_formulas.integral_form: ∫cos x/(1+sin x) dx = log|1+sin x| + c

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Separate variables, integrate both sides recognising each as a log|f| form, combine using log laws to get the product form of the solution.
logical_steps: Step 1: Rearrange to separate x and y terms
Step 2: Integrate the left side ∫cos x/(1+sin x) dx
Step 3: Integrate the right side ∫sin y/(1+cos y) dy
Step 5: Exponentiate to get the general solution

step_1_separate.rearrange: cos x(1+cos y) dx = sin y(1+sin x) dy
step_1_separate.separate: cos x/(1+sin x) dx = sin y/(1+cos y) dy

step_2_integrate_LHS.note: d/dx(1+sin x) = cos x → numerator is derivative of denominator

step_3_integrate_RHS.note: d/dy(1+cos y) = -sin y → sin y = -d/dy(1+cos y)

phase_5_verify_answer.answer: C. (1 + sin x)(1 + cos y) = c
phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Differentiating (1+sin x)(1+cos y)=c: (1+cos y)cos x dx + (1+sin x)(-sin y) dy = 0 → cos x(1+cos y) dx - sin y(1+sin x) dy = 0 ✓
